Museum Specimen Labels

A quiet gallery where every caught anomaly becomes a curated exhibit: a specimen under glass, pinned in coral, with a crisp wall label — catalogue number, italic title, three lines of context and "Discovered by Acme Pulse". Calm, airy and exact; the camera dollies from exhibit to exhibit, one per bar.

COMPONENT KIT

  • Specimen — the anomalous chart fragment presented under glass, the way a museum shows one object.
  • Wall label — catalogue number, italic serif title, a meta line and three lines of context, plus the action buttons.
  • Catalogue code — mono IDs ("PL-2231") that tie the exhibit to the deploy or event.
  • Coral pin — a single coral pin with a real shadow marking the exact moment of the drop.
  • Vitrine & plinth — thin glass case with reflection gradient on a pale plinth.
  • Wall vinyl & wayfinding — serif headlines applied to the wall, mono gallery signs ("Exhibit 1 · Caught in time").

MOTION · MUSIC

  • Rail slide — labels enter sideways 40 px, power3.out 500 ms, landing on a downbeat at 120 BPM.
  • Spotlight — a radial light brightens the specimen over 800 ms, sine.inOut, starting on beat 1 of each exhibit.
  • Wall pan — slow dolly between exhibits, exactly one exhibit per bar (2 s), eased with power1.inOut so cuts stay on the grid.

WHY / RISK · ADAPT IT

Curating a caught error as an exhibit reframes monitoring as care and craft: calm, confident and extremely readable. The label format forces you to say what, when, why and who decided in three lines. Risk: gallery pace can feel slow — every move must still land on the beat.

Adapt to your product: treat each thing your product catches or creates (a bug, a lead, a saved hour) as an exhibit, with a screenshot as the specimen and your own data in the label's three lines.
